players.product: Exensio yield / manufacturing analytics and DFI for fabs

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Adnan Raza (non-GAAP): Q2 total revenue was $61.5 million, up 19% year over year; first-half revenue grew 22% year over year on contributions from multiple products. Platform revenue was $49.1 million, up 14% versus Q2 of last year and up 24% for the six-month year-to-date period, helped by the DirectScan booking with a new non-leading-edge customer. Volume-based revenue rose 45% versus Q2 of last year, driven by strong Gainshare and Cimetrix runtime licenses.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $61.5 million (+19% YoY); H1 +22%; platform revenue $49.1 million (+14%, H1 +24%); volume-based revenue +45%

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: management reconfirmed 20% year-over-year revenue growth for full year 2026 versus 2025 (CEO John Kibarian, citing increased opportunities across the entire product portfolio in the second half; CFO citing bookings momentum in the deal pipeline). CFO: the company remains committed to its long-term 20% revenue growth target and its 27% target operating margin model; it expects gross margin to increase next quarter toward prior-quarter levels and has line of sight to its long-term 77% gross margin target model, which it aims to reach faster than the roughly two years the previous targets took.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue growth 20% reaffirmed; long-term targets: 20% revenue growth, 77% gross margin, 27% operating margin

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: total backlog grew to $271 million, up 10% versus last quarter and up 16% versus Q2 of last year; it does not include potential future Cimetrix runtime licenses or Gainshare revenue, so backlog would be higher with estimates of those amounts. Based on its pipeline the company anticipates strong bookings momentum in the second half and expects to grow backlog as it exits the year. CEO: backlog growth came partly from new customers (the DirectScan contract) and, as usual, a good chunk from existing customers.

Q2 bookings (CEO John Kibarian): secureWISE and DirectScan each booked eight-figure contracts; several seven-figure contracts for Exensio products and services, including with hyperscalers and photonics companies, as AI-ecosystem growth stays strong; Cimetrix bookings reached a record high on top of a very strong Q1 as the equipment industry stays robust. CEO: selling activity was very high from hyperscalers to equipment vendors, with significant activity in characterization and DirectScan systems as customers develop advanced processes and nodes, which management anticipates will result in strong bookings in that category as the year progresses.
quarterly_data.figure: eight-figure secureWISE and DirectScan contracts; multiple seven-figure Exensio contracts; record Cimetrix bookings

quarterly_data.signal: secureWISE: the eight-figure Q2 contract, with an existing equipment-company customer, is the largest in secureWISE's history that management is aware of; it commits that customer across all 300 mm fabs for a number of years at a minimum value, and both sides anticipate building from this base. CEO: the company has now refreshed the largest secureWISE contracts and expanded secureWISE services to front-end fabs and to back-end test and assembly facilities; the majority of secureWISE revenue already comes from data transmission across the network; more of the network's activity will become AI agents; management thinks secureWISE can grow at least at the company growth rate over the next few years.
quarterly_data.figure: eight-figure contract, largest in secureWISE history; all 300 mm fabs

quarterly_data.signal: eProbe / DirectScan: PDF placed three new eProbe e-beam inspection machines in Q2: two with new customers (one an evaluation, one a five-year subscription) and one at a new factory of an existing customer under a previously signed contract; with the Q1 shipment that is two-thirds of the way to the year's goal. The five-year subscription customer uses DirectScan on a more mature process node, which CEO John Kibarian says demonstrates DirectScan's value in mature nodes; the evaluation takes PDF into the memory market, which he calls an important beachhead, while noting such evaluations typically take close to a year to convert and declining to speculate on when or if it will. CEO: the DirectScan customer set (once described as five to 10 customers) is expanding and is 'definitely bigger than what we thought'; geographic expansion will be looked at later this year or early next year; 2027 production targets may be communicated by later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: three eProbe machines placed in Q2; two-thirds of the 2026 goal; five-year subscription

quarterly_data.signal: CEO John Kibarian on eProbe supply: capacity is not yet a limit and suppliers can build at a higher level than this; the biggest issue has been timeline and the supply chain, and costs keep rising for the computing element of the system given where memory prices are going, so PDF is working to make its costs more effective. CFO: higher component costs to meet DirectScan demand are part of the higher year-over-year capex.

CFO Adnan Raza: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 73%, lower than Q1 partly because Q1 had higher perpetual software licenses; operating expenses rose only 5% year over year; operating margin was 22%, about 300 basis points higher than a year earlier; EPS was $0.27, up 42% year over year and up 49% year to date. Operating cash flow was $16.4 million and capex $14.1 million, mainly for eProbe tools and long-lead items for future shipments; capex is expected to be incrementally higher in each of Q3 and Q4, with full-year average quarterly capex similar to Q2, and the company expects to end the year with a higher cash balance than in Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 73%; operating margin 22%; EPS $0.27 (+42%); operating cash flow $16.4 million; capex $14.1 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO John Kibarian: semiconductor investment continues to be driven by the unprecedented build-out of AI data centers; while it is debatable where the industry is in the demand cycle, he believes it is in the very early stages of the AI transformation of semiconductor manufacturing and engineering, and all supply-chain participants will need AI agents to be more nimble, innovative and cost-effective.

connects_to.relationship: secureWISE remote-connectivity platform standardized across Intel fabs

contracts.signal: CEO John Kibarian: last year PDF signed a large contract with Intel, which standardized on secureWISE, including for Intel's own internal use; Intel makes secureWISE available to any equipment vendor wanting remote access at Intel, provides a minimal level through that contract and directs equipment vendors that want to transmit more data or offer AI-driven solutions to PDF; Intel has also started making it available in back-end test and assembly.
